newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: ANOTHER AUSTRALIAN WANTS THE RIGHT TO DIE
A South Australian woman has gone public with her wish to become the second person to die under the Northern Territory voluntary euthanasia law.
52 year-old Janet Mills from Narracourt told a press conference in Darwin a short time ago she is suffering a terminal form of cancer.
But she says she lacks the signature of the specialist required under the Act to allow her to end her life.
APRA ARGUES TELSTRA SHOULD PAY COPYRIGHT
The High Court has been told it must decide whether telephone users automatically subscribe to all Telstra's services when they establish their accounts.
The Australasian Performing Right Association says they do, and as a result subscribe to Telstra's music on hold as part of a general communication service.
APRA is arguing by providing music on hold Telstra breaches the copyright act and should pay fees for the use of material.
However Telstra says the Act doesn't support APRA's argument and has called on the judges to reject the case. - - - -
ACCOUNTANTS SAY TAX SYSTEM REACHES LIMIT
The Institute of Chartered Accountants says Australia's tax system has reached the limits of its design capabilities.
The Institute has today released a report on tax reform written by Dr Neil Warren of the University of New South Wales.
The study examines the arguments for and against a broad-based consumption tax.
The Institute says Australians are consuming more services, while the relative demand for goods is dropping.
It says if there continues to be a trend towards greater consumption of untaxed services, the imbalance will become increasingly unsustainable.
SWIM STAR BRANCHES OUT
Swimming star Hayley Lewis has announced she will compete in triathalon events
Lewis, a winner of seven Commonweath games gold medals, is to take part in the final two rounds of the five round triathalon Grand Prix series in March.
She says she wants to continue preparing for next year's swimming world championships, but may choose triathalon as her next sport now that it enjoys Olympic status.
DEMOCRATS SAY DEAL IS A WIN FOR HEALTH SYSTEM
The Democrats say changes it's negotiated with the Federal Government over doctor numbers and training, will improve the health system.
As part of the deal under which the Democrats will support a plan to limit the number of new GPs, the Government will provide 250 more training places for junior doctors in rural Australia.
Democrats Health spokeswoman Meg Lees says a system will also be introduced where doctors who can't find a training place can join a register and be matched with available places.
If they still can't find a training place, they'll be offered training in a rural area under a six year country employment scheme.
